subject: Gaussian process in a multi-level ordinal logistic model

messages.author: 5d67cef991a09367
messages.subject: Gaussian process in a multi-level ordinal logistic model
parts:
Hello dear list,

I'm trying (unsuccesfully) to fit this multi-level model with a Gaussian process using the generalized squared exponential as described in the manual (see code and error message below). 

data{
    int<lower=1> N;
int<lower=1> N_CageID;
int<lower=1> N_sample;
int histo[N];
int CageID[N];
int sample[N];
vector[N_sample] weeks;
}

transformed data{
vector[N_sample] mu_sample;
for (i in 1:N_sample) mu_sample[i]=0;


}

parameters{
ordered[3] cutpoints;
real a;
vector[N_CageID] a_cage;
vector[N_sample] a_sample;
real<lower=0> sigma_cage;
real<lower=0> eta_sq;
real<lower=0> inv_rho_sq;
real<lower=0> sigma_sq;

}

transformed parameters{
real<lower=0> rho_sq;
  rho_sq = inv(inv_rho_sq);
}

model{
matrix[N_sample,N_sample] SIGMA_Dmat;
vector[N] phi;
a ~ normal( 0 , 10 );
sigma_cage ~ cauchy( 0 , 1 );
cutpoints ~ normal( 0 , 10 );

for ( i in 1:N ) {
phi[i] = a + a_cage[CageID[i]] + a_sample[sample[i]];
}
for ( i in 1:N )
histo[i] ~ ordered_logistic( phi[i] , cutpoints );


for (i in 1:(N_sample-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):N_sample) {
      SIGMA_Dmat[i, j] = eta_sq * exp(-rho_sq * pow(weeks[i] - weeks[j],2));
      SIGMA_Dmat[j, i] = SIGMA_Dmat[i, j];
    }
  }
for (k in 1:N_sample)
    SIGMA_Dmat[k, k] = eta_sq + sigma_sq; // + jitter

sigma_sq ~ cauchy( 0 , 5 );
inv_rho_sq ~ cauchy( 0 , 5 );
eta_sq ~ cauchy( 0 , 5 );


a_sample ~ multi_normal( mu_sample , SIGMA_Dmat );
a_cage ~ normal( 0 , sigma_cage );


}
generated quantities{
matrix[N_sample,N_sample] SIGMA_Dmat;
vector[N] phi;
real dev;
dev = 0;
for ( i in 1:N ) {
phi[i] = a + a_cage[CageID[i]] + a_sample[sample[i]];
}
for ( i in 1:N )
dev = dev + (-2)*ordered_logistic_lpmf( histo[i] | phi[i] , cutpoints );
}


Error in validObject(.Object) : 
  invalid class “stanfit” object: The following variables have undefined values:  SIGMA_Dmat[1,1],The following variables have undefined values:  SIGMA_Dmat[2,1],The following variables have undefined values:  SIGMA_Dmat[3,1],The following variables have undefined values:  SIGMA_Dmat[4,1],The following variables have undefined values:  SIGMA_Dmat[5,1]

Then, I tried fitting just the gaussian process outside the multi-level model (see code below), and it seems to work fine. Is the error I'm getting because of the multi-level structure? likelihood function (cum logit)? or both?
Thanks for any advice hints you might have,

Tada


data {
  int<lower=1> N_sample;
  vector[N_sample] weeks;
  
}
transformed data {
  vector[N_sample] mu;
  for (i in 1:N_sample) mu[i] = 0;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> eta_sq;
  real<lower=0> inv_rho_sq;
  real<lower=0> sigma_sq;
vector [N_sample] a_sample;
}
transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> rho_sq;
  rho_sq = inv(inv_rho_sq);
}
model {
  matrix[N_sample, N_sample] Sigma;
  // off-diagonal elements
  for (i in 1:(N_sample-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):N_sample) {
      Sigma[i, j] = eta_sq * exp(-rho_sq * pow(weeks[i] - weeks[j],2));
      Sigma[j, i] = Sigma[i, j];
    }
  }
  // diagonal elements
  for (k in 1:N_sample)
    Sigma[k, k] = eta_sq + sigma_sq; // + jitter
  eta_sq ~ cauchy(0, 5);
  inv_rho_sq ~ cauchy(0, 5);
  sigma_sq ~ cauchy(0, 5);
  a_sample ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

messages.author: 61924cbc2e733aae
messages.subject: Re: Gaussian process in a multi-level ordinal logistic model
parts:
Hi Tadaishi:

I think that probably what happen is that your covariance matrix `SIGMA_Dmat` is define in the model block, so is a local variable that your generate quantities block don't see.

You need to define the covariance matrix in the transformed parameters block.

Regards.

Álvaro.
